A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same dynamic k-center research despite the changed title and expanded author list. All pages, mathematical material and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 presents algorithms, theoretical guarantees and proofs, including a literature-comparison table in Appendix A. It reports no original empirical results.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical throughout the main text and Appendices A–C. Randomized algorithm analyses and theoretical comparison bounds are not empirical results.

M1.justification: The nested-MIS construction is retained, but the sparsifier changes: AlmostCover covers one-quarter rather than one-half of its input, and reconstruction selects the best of Theta(log n) independent calls. New Appendix C introduces BufferedSparsifier with snapshots, lazy updates and periodic resets, plus a variant retaining deleted centers when permitted.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical training/evaluation tasks. Appendix C adds a theoretical setting allowing centers outside the current input, without evaluating it experimentally.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparison methods. Appendix A retains the same four prior-work comparators and their theoretical guarantees.

E3.justification: Neither version contains experimental protocols or evaluation settings. Changes to sampling and reconstruction are algorithmic procedures, not experimental settings.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, empirical robustness tests, sensitivity studies or case studies. The added appendices supply theoretical arguments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run statistics, confidence intervals or significance tests. Expectations, high-probability guarantees and repeated sampling concern randomized algorithms and their proofs.

E6.justification: Neither PDF reports empirical result entries or observed performance findings. Changes to numerical approximation, recourse and running-time guarantees are theoretical changes assessed under T1 and C1.

T1.justification: v2 replaces v1's norm-comparison argument for an unspecified constant approximation with a direct sparsifier analysis targeting factor 4. It generalizes the composition theorem, expands the recourse and running-time arguments, proves the previously used subset-optimum inequality in Appendix B, and adds buffered-sparsifier guarantees and proofs in Appendix C.

C1.justification: The central claim of constant approximation and recourse with near-linear-in-k update time remains. v2 specifies a final approximation factor of 20 and O(k log^5(n) log Delta) update time, and advertises an 8 + epsilon recourse variant. The underlying algorithm's approximation factor 8 and recourse bound 4 already appeared in v1's analysis.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly explains how buffering controls recourse despite the original sparsifier's potentially large hidden constant. Remark C.4 explicitly conditions the 4 + epsilon recourse variant on allowing centers outside the current dynamic input, adding a substantive applicability distinction.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands operational detail: Section 2.3 explains distance computations and binary-search-tree maintenance; Algorithm 1 specifies reconstruction counters, repeated sampling and stopping conditions; Appendix C specifies buffering parameters and reset/reporting behavior. These replace several high-level implementation descriptions in v1.

R1.justification: Related work expands to memory-efficient clustering, doubling metrics, graph updates and newer dynamic k-median research, adding Chan et al. (2022), Gan and Golin (2024), Cruciani et al. (2024), Pellizzoni et al. (2025) and Bhattacharya et al. (2025). Braverman et al. (2016) and Gupta and Tangwongsan (2008) disappear. The central positioning around Bateni's algorithm and Bhattacharya's sparsifier remains.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title and author list, consolidates definitions into a preliminaries subsection, reorganizes Section 3 and expands several explanations. It adds concluding and administrative sections. Much of the introduction, technical overview and original proof narrative remains recognizable; most substantial new text accompanies scientific additions.

P2.justification: The single-column manuscript becomes a two-column conference paper with running headers and full-width appendices. v2 adds a displayed pseudocode algorithm and reformats Table 1, moving its caption and removing the 'Our Result' row while retaining the four prior-work rows.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through fuller analysis and implementation detail, but its new Appendix C relies on a problematic lemma. Under the paper's requirement that centers belong to the input, Lemma C.1 fails: if V comprises three leaves of a unit-edge star and V' adds its center, OPT_2(V)=2 exceeds OPT_1(V')=1 despite one update. This leaves the buffered-variant proof unsupported as written. Lemma 3.3 also states a stronger sparsifier time bound than Lemma 3.13 derives. These substantial additions and correctness concerns prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
